label: EU AI Act Article 73 serious incident reporting
authority: Market surveillance authority of the member state where the incident occurred
citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 73 (definitions in Article 3(49) and 3(61)); application dates in Article 113 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L, 24.7.2026, EUR-Lex
AI Act Article 73 text, AI Act Service Desk and Future of Life Institute explorer

statusNote: Binds providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market; deployers give the provider the information. A company defrauded by a deepfake, with no AI system of its own involved, has a fraud and cyber incident, not an Article 73 incident. This is not legal advice: check which of your own plans and which role (provider, deployer or victim) applies. Article 73 (Chapter IX) applies from 2 August 2026 under Article 113, second paragraph, and Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 did not change it. That amending regulation (OJ L, 24.7.2026, in force 27 July 2026) moved Chapter III, Sections 1 to 3 (classification as high-risk, requirements and provider obligations, except Article 6(5)) to 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems, so a system is a high-risk system with these duties from those dates.

triggers.label: Provider became aware of a serious incident
triggers.hint: Any serious incident of a high-risk system. Report immediately after the causal link is established or reasonably likely.

triggers.label: Provider became aware of a widespread infringement or a critical infrastructure incident
triggers.hint: A widespread infringement (Article 3(61)) or a serious incident of the kind in Article 3(49)(b).

triggers.label: Provider became aware of a death
triggers.hint: Start when the provider is aware of the death and a causal relationship is established or suspected.

clocks.label: Serious incident report (15 days)
clocks.rule: Immediately after the causal link is established or reasonably likely, and in any event not later than 15 days after the provider becomes aware. An incomplete initial report is allowed, followed by a complete one.

clocks.label: Widespread infringement or critical infrastructure report (2 days)
clocks.rule: Immediately, and not later than two days after the provider becomes aware. An incomplete initial report is allowed.

clocks.label: Death report (10 days)
clocks.rule: Immediately once a causal relationship is established or suspected, and not later than 10 days after the provider becomes aware of the death.

dates.label: General date of application, including Article 73 (Chapter IX)
dates.note: Article 113, second paragraph, of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (OJ L, 12.7.2024); not amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Checked against the Official Journal text on 2026-11-05.

dates.label: Chapter III, Sections 1 to 3 apply to Annex III (Article 6(2)) high-risk systems
dates.note: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1(40)(b) (OJ L, 24.7.2026). Checked against the Official Journal text on 2026-11-05.

dates.label: Chapter III, Sections 1 to 3 apply to Annex I (Article 6(1)) high-risk systems
dates.note: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 1(40)(b) (OJ L, 24.7.2026). Checked against the Official Journal text on 2026-11-05.

appliesTo.note: Providers of high-risk AI systems. Choose the scenario role (provider, deployer, victim of fraud) before using these clocks.
